correctness.rationale: The claim is true for the stated intrinsic (not Euclidean) graph Čech convention. From the actual package, independently construct Q4 via Hamming-distance-one graph, all 32 edge neighborhoods N1[u]∪N1[v], and every nonempty subface: exactly 3944 simplices and f-vector (16,112,448,1016,1264,800,256,32). Independently reimplement the stated staged 16-vertex toggle matching, obtaining 1959 disjoint Hasse pairs, verifying all 18800 covers and acyclicity by a fresh DFS over the complete oriented Hasse digraph (3944 visited). Exactly one 0-cell, one 3-cell and 24 4-cells remain. Fresh iterative integer gradient-path propagation on all 1264 four-dimensional cells yields all 24 signed Morse boundary coefficients equal to zero. Forman Morse equivalence plus degree classification π3(S3)=Z then yields S3∨(∨24 S4). The cross-check is exhaustive for this finite Q4 complex, not an infinite-family proof. This directly supports the submitted correctness, irrespective of originality.

evidence: Theorem 5.9: N(I_n,3) is 5-collapsible for every n≥4; Proposition 5.4: a 5-collapsible complex has a homotopy-equivalent model of dimension <5.
Lemma 5.12: N(I_n,3) is 2-connected for all n≥2.
Table 1: at n=4, r=3 the integral reduced homology is Z in degree 3 and Z^24 in degree 4.
The six-cube finding computes n=6 and explicitly explains Smith reductions of 2-connected 3/4-dimensional Morse CW complexes; its n=6 numerical statement itself does not imply n=4.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The exact Q4 conclusion is ALREADY IMPLIED by published statements in Adams–Shukla–Singh. Their Theorem 5.9 plus Proposition 5.4 give a homotopy-equivalent finite CW model of dimension at most four for N(I_4,3); their Lemma 5.12 proves 2-connectedness; and their Table 1 states integral reduced H_3=Z and H_4=Z^24 with no other reduced homology. For any 2-connected finite four-dimensional CW complex Y with these free homology groups, its 3-skeleton Y^(3) is 2-connected and homotopy equivalent to a wedge of a copies of S^3 (Hurewicz plus simply-connected homology Whitehead). All 4-cell attaching maps are classified by degree vectors in π_3(∨^a S^3)=Z^a, forming precisely the integer cellular ∂_4 matrix. The free cokernel H_3=Z forces every nonzero Smith invariant to equal 1, with matrix rank a−1; the kernel H_4=Z^24 determines the remaining 24 four-cells. Elementary unimodular changes of bases and cancellation of unit 3/4-cell pairs give Y≃S^3∨(∨^24 S^4). Thus this published dimension/connectivity/homology combination *mathematically forces* the submitted wedge, although the paper describes the particular table cell as not explicitly known up to homotopy. This is a previously available consequence, not a new unresolved homotopy invariant.

This provides interpretive and computational value even though its particular wedge type follows as a standard corollary of earlier published structural results. That earlier implication defeats originality and prevents acceptance, irrespective of the interest of the independent explicit certificate.
